episode_title: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur
question: What mental health challenges do Black entrepreneurs face while building their business?
transcript_excerpt: Black entrepreneurs face compounded pressure from being Black in America and simultaneously running a business. This adds a different arsenal of pressure, making it easy to get wrapped up in proving haters wrong and goal orientation to the point of neglecting eating, sleeping, and taking breaks, especially when working a nine-to-five job while running a side business.

episode_title: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur
question: How can business owners prevent mental health breakdowns from overwork and stress?
transcript_excerpt: Business owners should take time away from the grind to keep themselves aligned and in check. This can be as simple as taking a day off and laying in bed, spending time with family or friends, or going to places that bring you back to reality and keep you grounded. Setting firm boundaries is essential, including not responding to anyone on designated days off and communicating this to customers in advance.

episode_title: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur
question: Why should entrepreneurs celebrate small wins instead of only focusing on major goals?
transcript_excerpt: Small wins should be celebrated because they represent real progress and momentum. Enjoying small wins on the journey keeps morale high and creates memory markers that make achieving larger goals feel more rewarding. Additionally, when working in service-based industries dealing with different people daily, acknowledging progress like gaining one new customer or follower maintains motivation and prevents getting lost in pursuing only the end goal.

episode_title: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur
question: What scheduling strategy can entrepreneurs use when working both a nine-to-five job and a side business?
transcript_excerpt: Entrepreneurs should map out their schedule to give themselves a few hours to work on their business while also allocating hours to recover and reset. Another approach is working intensively for three days straight and taking the fourth day completely off to recharge. The key is planning deliberately rather than working 24/7, as the nine-to-five is the main income source until the business takes off.

episode_title: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur
question: How should Black entrepreneurs handle imposter syndrome and self-doubt while building their empire?
transcript_excerpt: Build your empire brick by brick and appreciate the incremental progress. If you lay down two bricks today, that is two more bricks than you had yesterday. Give yourself credit and recognize that building a business is difficult work that many people are not doing. Reflecting on growth from having five customers to fifty to five hundred helps combat self-doubt by documenting real progress.
